title: Quantum Electrodynamics
subtitle: A visual laboratory for quantum fields, operator algebras, noncommutative geometry, and renormalization

lenses.chain: algebra → Hilbert space → Dirac operator → inner fluctuations → action

lenses.name: Operator-algebraic QFT
lenses.chain: spacetime regions → local von Neumann algebras → modular structure

lensWarning: The three lenses are related but not identified: Connes–Kreimer renormalization organizes perturbative graphs, spectral triples encode geometry and the spectral action, and algebraic QFT studies nets of local von Neumann algebras. They share operator algebras, Hilbert spaces, symmetry and states; none is claimed to contain the others.

presentation.title: What is a quantum field?
presentation.caption: A field assigns a value to every spacetime point; the Dirac field ψ(x) needs a different encoding from a vector field.
presentation.narration: A field assigns a value to every point of spacetime. Scalars, the electromagnetic potential and the Dirac field need three different pictures.

presentation.title: QED Lagrangian
presentation.caption: Three terms: field energy, the free Dirac field, and the interaction eψ̄γ^μA_μψ.
presentation.narration: The QED Lagrangian has three terms. Each one changes the main picture: field energy, the free electron field, and the electron photon interaction.

presentation.title: Gauge symmetry
presentation.caption: ψ ↦ e^{−ieχ}ψ and A ↦ A + ∂χ together: phases rotate, the comparison through the connection does not.
presentation.narration: A local gauge transformation rotates the phase of the electron field at every point. The connection rotates with it, so the comparison of neighbouring phases is unchanged.

presentation.title: Quantizing field modes
presentation.caption: Fourier modes of a string are oscillators; quantizing each gives a quantum field.
presentation.narration: A vibrating string is a sum of Fourier modes. Each mode is an oscillator, and quantizing every oscillator gives a quantum field.

presentation.title: Fock space
presentation.caption: Sectors with 0, 1, 2, … particles; an interaction moves amplitude between sectors.
presentation.narration: Fock space is a sum of sectors with zero, one, two and more particles. An interaction moves amplitude from one sector to another.

presentation.title: Propagators
presentation.caption: S_F(p) = i(p̸ + m)/(p² − m² + iε) and D_μν(q) = −ig_μν/(q² + iε); the mass shell p² = m² is where the denominator vanishes.
presentation.narration: The electron and photon propagators have denominators that vanish on the mass shell. Internal lines need not lie on it.

presentation.title: Feynman diagrams
presentation.caption: Wick's theorem pairs fields into propagators; each pairing is a diagram.
presentation.narration: Wick's theorem turns a product of fields into a sum over pairings. Each pairing becomes a diagram whose lines are propagators.

presentation.title: Tree-level scattering
presentation.caption: e⁻μ⁻ → e⁻μ⁻ by one-photon exchange: the amplitude computed spin by spin.
presentation.narration: Electron muon scattering at tree level exchanges one photon. The page computes the amplitude for every spin and averages it.

presentation.title: Loop corrections
presentation.caption: At one loop: self-energy, vacuum polarization, vertex correction.
presentation.narration: At one loop there are three corrections: the electron self energy, vacuum polarization and the vertex correction.

presentation.title: UV divergence
presentation.caption: The cumulative loop integral keeps growing as the cutoff Λ rises: contributions from large |k|.
presentation.narration: The loop integral keeps growing as the cutoff rises. The growth comes from large loop momenta: an ultraviolet divergence.

presentation.title: Regularization
presentation.caption: In d = 4 − ε the integral becomes a Laurent series: pole, finite part, vanishing part.
presentation.narration: In four minus epsilon dimensions the integral becomes a Laurent series: a pole, a finite part and terms that vanish.

presentation.title: Running charge
presentation.caption: One-loop QED, MS-bar: 1/α(μ) falls by (2/3π) log μ.
presentation.narration: In one loop QED the coupling grows slowly with the scale, because vacuum polarization screens the bare charge less at short distance.

presentation.title: Wilsonian RG
presentation.caption: Integrate out a momentum shell, rescale, and the couplings move.
presentation.narration: Wilson's view integrates out a shell of high momenta, rescales, and watches the couplings move.

presentation.title: Hopf algebra of graphs
presentation.caption: 1PI graphs become generators of a commutative Hopf algebra; the product is disjoint union.
presentation.narration: Connes and Kreimer turn one particle irreducible graphs into the generators of a Hopf algebra whose product is disjoint union.

presentation.title: Coproduct and forests
presentation.caption: ΔΓ = Γ⊗1 + 1⊗Γ + ∑ γ⊗Γ/γ: each divergent subgraph is pulled out and contracted.
presentation.narration: The coproduct pulls out each divergent subgraph and contracts it. Its terms are the subtraction terms of the forest formula.

presentation.title: Birkhoff decomposition
presentation.caption: γ = γ₋^{−1}γ₊: counterterms from the pole part, the renormalized value γ₊(0).
presentation.narration: The regularized Feynman rules give a loop of characters, and the Birkhoff decomposition splits it into counterterms and a renormalized part.

presentation.title: Renormalization as Riemann–Hilbert
presentation.caption: A loop around ε = 0 on the Riemann sphere, factored into the inside and outside pieces.
presentation.narration: On the Riemann sphere, the loop around epsilon equals zero factors into a piece holomorphic inside and a piece holomorphic outside.

presentation.title: Algebra as geometry
presentation.caption: Points become characters of C^∞(M); then commutativity is dropped.
presentation.narration: Points of a space become characters of its algebra of functions. Noncommutative geometry then drops commutativity.

presentation.title: Spectral triples
presentation.caption: (𝒜, ℋ, D): algebra, Hilbert space, Dirac operator; the manifold fades, the data remain.
presentation.narration: A spectral triple is an algebra, a Hilbert space and a Dirac operator. Much of the geometry can be recovered from these data.

presentation.title: Connes distance
presentation.caption: d(x, y) = sup{|f(x) − f(y)| : ‖[D, f]‖ ≤ 1}: the supremum rises to the geodesic distance.
presentation.narration: Connes' distance searches over functions whose commutator with the Dirac operator has norm at most one. The supremum is the geodesic distance.

presentation.title: Inner fluctuations
presentation.caption: D ↦ D + A + JAJ⁻¹ puts a U(1) phase on every link; particle and antiparticle copies carry opposite charge.
presentation.narration: An inner fluctuation adds a one form to the Dirac operator. In the doubled model the link phases are a U of one gauge field with opposite charges.

presentation.title: Spectral action
presentation.caption: Tr f(D_A/Λ) weighs eigenvalues; low ones count, high ones are suppressed.
presentation.narration: The spectral action weighs each eigenvalue of the fluctuated Dirac operator by a cutoff function and adds them up.

presentation.title: Local observable algebras
presentation.caption: O ↦ 𝒜(O): nested regions give nested algebras, spacelike regions commute.
presentation.narration: Algebraic QFT assigns an algebra of observables to each region. Nested regions give nested algebras and spacelike regions give commuting ones.

presentation.title: Type III factors
presentation.caption: Type I has minimal projections, type II a trace, type III neither: local algebras are of type III.
presentation.narration: Type one algebras have minimal projections, type two have a trace, and type three have neither. Local algebras in relativistic QFT are of type three.

presentation.title: Modular theory
presentation.caption: S = JΔ^{1/2}; Δ^{it} moves observables: dynamics from algebra and state.
presentation.narration: The Tomita operator splits as J times the square root of Delta. Delta to the i t then moves observables: a flow from the algebra and the state alone.

presentation.title: Anomaly and spectral flow
presentation.caption: As the gauge field varies, Dirac eigenvalues cross zero; the net count is an index.
presentation.narration: As the gauge field changes, eigenvalues of the Dirac operator cross zero. Their net count is an index, which underlies the axial anomaly.

presentation.title: Grand synthesis
presentation.caption: Spacetime, perturbation, NCG, local algebras: related concepts, never declared identical.
presentation.narration: Quantum field theory can be read as fields on spacetime, operator algebras, spectral geometry and combinatorial renormalization.

ontologies.name: Fields
ontologies.emu: Interacting Dirac currents j^μ_e = ψ̄_eγ^μψ_e and j^μ_μ coupled through the electromagnetic field A_μ.

ontologies.name: Particles
ontologies.emu: Incoming and outgoing asymptotic electron and muon states |p₁, p₂⟩ → |p₃, p₄⟩.

ontologies.name: Graphs
ontologies.emu: The one-photon-exchange diagram: a term in the perturbative expansion, not a movie.

ontologies.name: Operators
ontologies.emu: The S-matrix element ⟨p₃p₄|S|p₁p₂⟩, obtained from time-ordered correlation functions by the LSZ formula.

real.name: field configuration
real.status: A classical field configuration is a point in the space the path integral sums over; in the quantum theory the field is an operator-valued distribution, not a definite configuration.

real.name: particle state
real.status: A particle is an asymptotic state: a vector in Fock space (or the scattering states of the interacting theory), defined by how it transforms under the Poincaré group.

real.name: observable algebra
real.status: In algebraic QFT the net O ↦ 𝒜(O) is the primary object; states and particles are derived from it.

real.name: Feynman graph
real.status: Feynman diagrams are terms in a perturbative expansion, not literal microscopic movies.

real.name: virtual line
real.status: An internal line is a propagator inside an amplitude. Its momentum need not satisfy p² = m²; it is not a particle that briefly exists, and energy–momentum is conserved at every vertex.

real.name: renormalization scale
real.status: μ is a bookkeeping choice. Physical predictions do not depend on it; truncated perturbative results depend on it weakly, which the RG organizes.

questions: What are the fields and symmetries?
What operator algebra do the observables generate?
What spectral geometry is encoded by the theory?
constraints: Feynman diagrams are never drawn as spacetime histories.
Internal lines are propagators; nothing 'temporarily violates energy conservation'.
Counterterms are not arbitrary: symmetry (the Ward identity) constrains them.
The spectrum of a general operator is not only its eigenvalues.
QFT is not identified with perturbation theory.
Spectral triples, Connes–Kreimer renormalization and AQFT are not one formalism.
Local algebras are not claimed to be the same factor without hypotheses.
NCG does not mean physical coordinates fail to commute.
The spectral Standard Model is not a complete nonperturbative quantization.
The bare coupling is never shown as measurable.
Numerical running always carries its loop order and scheme.

prereqs.label: linear algebra
prereqs.explainer: Vectors add and scale; matrices act on them. Eigenvectors are the directions a matrix only stretches.

prereqs.label: Hilbert spaces
prereqs.explainer: A vector space with an inner product, complete under its norm: ℓ² sequences and L² functions are the examples QFT needs.

prereqs.label: unbounded operators
prereqs.explainer: Operators like d/dx or a Hamiltonian are defined only on a dense domain; their spectra are unbounded.

prereqs.label: spectral theorem
prereqs.explainer: A self-adjoint operator is multiplication by a real function after a change of basis: its spectrum may be discrete, continuous or both.

prereqs.label: group theory
prereqs.explainer: Symmetries compose and invert: a group. Rotations of a phase form U(1).

prereqs.label: Lie groups
prereqs.explainer: Smooth groups such as U(1) and SU(2), linearized near the identity by their Lie algebras.

prereqs.label: gauge theory
prereqs.explainer: A Lie group acting independently at every point, with a connection to compare neighbouring points.

prereqs.label: complex analysis
prereqs.explainer: Holomorphic functions are determined by their values on curves; poles and residues govern contour integrals.

prereqs.label: Laurent series
prereqs.explainer: Near a pole, f(ε) = a₋₁/ε + a₀ + a₁ε + …: the negative powers are the pole part.

prereqs.label: Riemann–Hilbert
prereqs.explainer: Factor a loop of matrices on a circle into a piece holomorphic inside and a piece holomorphic outside.

prereqs.label: renormalization
prereqs.explainer: Absorb divergences into redefined parameters so that predictions in terms of measured quantities are finite.

prereqs.label: algebras
prereqs.explainer: Vector spaces with an associative product: matrices, functions, operators.

prereqs.label: C*-algebras
prereqs.explainer: Normed *-algebras with ‖a*a‖ = ‖a‖²: the abstract home of bounded observables.

prereqs.label: von Neumann algebras
prereqs.explainer: *-algebras of operators equal to their bicommutant M = M″, closed in the weak topology.

prereqs.label: modular theory
prereqs.explainer: A faithful state on a von Neumann algebra defines a canonical one-parameter group of automorphisms.

prereqs.label: Hopf algebras
prereqs.explainer: Algebras with a compatible coproduct and antipode: they encode how objects split into parts.

prereqs.label: graph coproduct
prereqs.explainer: ΔΓ = Γ⊗1 + 1⊗Γ + ∑ γ⊗Γ/γ: every way to cut a subdivergence out of a graph.

prereqs.label: Connes–Kreimer
prereqs.explainer: Feynman rules are characters of the graph Hopf algebra, and renormalization is their Birkhoff decomposition.

prereqs.label: Riemannian geometry
prereqs.explainer: Manifolds with a metric: lengths, angles, curvature.

prereqs.label: spinors / Dirac operator
prereqs.explainer: On a spin manifold the Dirac operator is a square root of the Laplacian (plus curvature), acting on spinor fields.

prereqs.label: spectral triples
prereqs.explainer: (𝒜, ℋ, D): an algebra acting on a Hilbert space with a Dirac-type operator of compact resolvent.

prereqs.label: NCG
prereqs.explainer: Geometry read from operator-algebraic and spectral data, including when the algebra does not commute.

prereqChains: linear algebra → Hilbert spaces → unbounded operators → spectral theorem
group theory → Lie groups → gauge theory
complex analysis → Laurent series → Riemann–Hilbert → renormalization
algebras → C*-algebras → von Neumann algebras → modular theory
Riemannian geometry → spinors / Dirac operator → spectral triples → NCG

finale.text: An electron moving through spacetime.
Zoom out: it becomes a Dirac field.
Quantize it: operators on Fock space.
Introduce the interaction.
Expand perturbatively: a Feynman graph appears.
Add a loop: a UV divergence appears.
Zoom into the graph: divergent subgraphs separate.
They become terms of a Hopf coproduct.
The regularized Feynman rule becomes a loop of characters.
The loop winds around ε = 0.
It splits.
The finite part becomes the renormalized amplitude.
Spacetime dissolves into spectral data.
The Dirac operator fluctuates.
The electromagnetic potential reappears.
Zoom out: a spacetime region is selected.
Its observables form a local algebra.
The algebra is of type III.
With the vacuum Ω, the Tomita operator splits.
Modular flow begins.

finaleWords: Quantum field theory can be read simultaneously as
fields on spacetime, operator algebras, spectral geometry, and combinatorial renormalization.
Connes' viewpoint asks how much of geometry and physics can be reconstructed from algebra, spectrum and symmetry.
Feynman graphs show perturbative quantum dynamics.
Hopf algebras expose the geometry of renormalization.
Spectral triples turn geometry into operator data.
Von Neumann algebras encode local quantum observables.
Modular theory exposes hidden dynamical structure.
